subject: MSA + Order Form: indemnity redlines and sig path
messages:
From: Samantha Yates <samantha@novahealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, procurement@novahealth.com
Cc: Patricia Kim <patricia.kim@novalegal.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: indemnity redlines and sig path

Jonas / Redwood legal,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to move forward. Our GC has put redlines on the MSA and Order Form focusing on indemnity. High level asks:

- Replace "right to defend" with a reimbursement-only position for alleged IP infringement tied to model outputs.
- Add a carveout that customer-generated fine-tuning data (and its outputs) are excluded from any Redwood indemnity obligations.
- Limit any remedy to direct damages only and request a $250k cap per claim.

We attached the redlined MSA (Nova_MSA_redlines_v3.docx). Can you confirm:
1) Whether Redwood can accept a defend-right carve for customer-provided data and training sets,
2) An evidence / notice timeline that works for you if a claim arises, and
3) A realistic sig path — procurement wants a DocuSign-ready set by 6/10 to hit their quarter close.

If it helps, Patel in procurement is on copy to coordinate contracting. Patricia (counsel) is ours and will be reviewing further.

Appreciate a short note on preferred options so we can map internal approvals.

Best,
Samantha
Director, Strategic Procurement
NovaHealth

Attachments: Nova_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (docx, redline)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yates <samantha@novahealth.com>
Cc: Patricia Kim <patricia.kim@novalegal.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: indemnity redlines and sig path

Samantha — thanks for the clear redlines and timeline. We reviewed with Legal and Sales; high-level response below. Please see our annotated redline (Redline_response_v1.docx) attached.

Quick answers to your three asks:
1) Customer-provided training data carveout: we are open to excluding data that is explicitly uploaded by NovaHealth and used only for fine-tuning for your private models. We need the Order Form to identify the datasets by name or bucket and a warranty that you have rights to that content.

2) Evidence / notice timeline: we can agree to a notice window of 30 days from first written notice for handing evidence and coordination, with an SLA to acknowledge receipt within 3 business days. We will require access to the specific prompt/output and any claim materials necessary for us to evaluate.

3) Sig path: we can target 6/10 but need a final redline by 6/7 to route for internal signoff.

Key legal positions we are holding: we will keep a right to participate in defense and, in certain cases, to control the defense for third-party IP claims that are directly tied to the model outputs we ship. For claims that stem from customer-provided content, we are prepared to accept reimbursement-only (subject to the warranty/attribution above).

Two trade proposals for your counsel to consider (both intended to bridge the defense vs. reimbursement gap):
- Option A (preferred): Redwood retains right to defend for model-output claims where the output is not primarily customer-origin content; Nova retains indemnity for infringements arising solely from customer-provided training data. Cap: $1,000,000 per claim, subject to insurance offset.
- Option B (fallback): Redwood offers reimbursement-only across the board but increases the cap to $2,000,000 and agrees to participate reasonably in evidence collection and settlement discussions.

If you want to move quickly, Option A will require a brief warranty clause identifying customer datasets + a short evidence-handback SLA (we've attached a draft XLSX).

Proposed next steps:
- Your legal flags which option you prefer and any non-starter language by 6/6.
- We exchange a final redline by 6/7.
- DocuSign envelope initiated 6/10 for signatures.

Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Ben (Sales) to keep internal track.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Commercial Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redline_response_v1.docx (docx, annotated); evidence-handback-sla.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Nova — negotiation points and fallback language

Internal only — do not forward to customer.

Jonas / Ben / Laura,

Key talking points I want captured in our final redline and negotiation script:

1) Definition clarity: add a short definition for "Customer Data for Fine-Tuning" that requires an explicit list in the Order Form or an S3/GS bucket ID.
2) Evidence obligations: require Nova to preserve the exact prompt and output, metadata (model id, seed, timestamps), and a signed statement from their engineering lead confirming dataset provenance.
3) Joint defense: carve the "right to defend" so Redwood can elect to defend where the claim alleges Redwood-delivered output infringes third-party IP independent of customer-provided content. If Redwood defends, Nova gets to appoint counsel and cooperate; Redwood will not settle without Nova's consent unless settlement releases Redwood only.
4) Insurance offset: any payout reduces claim amounts by reasonably available insurance proceeds; require both parties to reasonably pursue insurance as primary recovery.
5) Caps: recommend Option A with $1M cap per claim and an aggregate cap of $3M for the term to make it more acceptable to execs.

Fallback negotiation concessions we can offer:
- Shorten the notice window to 14 days if they agree to broaden our defense control for non-customer-data claims.
- Offer a carveout for claims arising from third-party model components (OSS) only if Nova accepts a higher cap.

I'll prepare suggested redline language for each point this afternoon. Once we have their preference between Option A/B, Sales can confirm commercial impact and we can route for signoff.

Kimberly
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

(Attachment: internal_draft_points.txt — internal briefing)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yates <samantha@novahealth.com>, Patricia Kim <patricia.kim@novalegal.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: indemnity redlines and sig path

Samantha / Patricia — thanks for the quick turnaround. Appreciate Patricia being on the thread.

Summary and agreed path:
- We prefer Option A as a starting point: Redwood reserves the right to defend third-party IP claims where the claim clearly ties to a Redwood-generated output that is not primarily customer-provided content.
- For claims arising from customer-provided training data/outputs (explicitly listed in the Order Form), Redwood will accept reimbursement-only, subject to Nova providing the dataset identifiers and a warranty of rights.
- Cap proposal: $1,000,000 per claim with an aggregate $3,000,000 term cap. We will include insurance offset language so available proceeds reduce Redwood's net exposure.
- Evidence and notice: 30-day notice to Redwood, Redwood to acknowledge in 3 business days. Nova to preserve original prompt/output and provide engineer attestation.

Attached is our final suggested redline (Redline_final_for_sig.docx). If that looks acceptable, can you confirm acceptance of Option A and confirm that procurement will start the DocuSign envelope on 6/10? If Nova needs the higher-cap fallback (Option B) please flag and we will escalate to Sales leadership for approval.

Next actions:
- Nova: confirm Option A/Option B and procurement's sig timeline (by EOD 6/6).
- Redwood: if Option A accepted, we will circulate the DocuSign-ready file and aim to route for signatures on 6/10.

Thanks — Jonas
Head of Commercial Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redline_final_for_sig.docx (docx, ready for signature)
